The working file is the complete analysis; the reports are its reader copies. Each should be read in full — this message is not the analysis.

In brief: the recommendation is conditional, not a flat yes or no. Do not launch a full, permanent free tier, and do not reject the idea outright either — run a single, capped, time-boxed, instrumented pilot (ICP-gated signups, nurture-track routing instead of the SDR queue, self-serve-only support, a 6-month/minimum-volume window, with numeric scale/kill thresholds set before launch, not after). The "competitors have one" argument carries no evidentiary weight once examined — it's discarded. A Fermi breakeven calculation shows the unit economics are structurally plausible given the $10k ACV (required conversion as low as 0.27%, as high as ~4% depending on cost containment), but the pivotal variables — non-ICP cost containment and real conversion — are genuinely unmeasured for this company. Confidence is MEDIUM throughout, capped because several inputs (the company's own figures, the finance cost model, and industry benchmarks) are unverified at source; the pilot itself is what would resolve that.
